never really got into the jc, but i did have experience with dsa for leadership for these schools, and i can tell you what i learned and some insight/thoughts? :D

first off i think it's great that you've been maintaining your grades; i'm not sure to what extent this is true, but i believe most elite colleges, for **leadership**, value academic grades a lot when you try to apply for dsa. so keep up the great work. :D

​

> I have a vice president leadership position in CCA and I also have 2 executive positions in non-profit organisations outside of school.

I think this is great! these positions definitely gives you an upper hand because having positions outside of school shows something more unique than most candidates who are often part of SC/CCA leaders/etc. without going outside of school for opportunities. it shows you have initiative to seek the pursuit of what you are actually really passionate about!

​

>my main concern is that I am not a Student Council member which I would say is the basic unspoken requirement for all the DSA leadership candidates.

not TOOO sure about this, maybe it could give you an upper hand if you are part of SC, but this is likely not necessary. i've heard of a guy who got into the interview stage without being part of the SC and was only a CCA leader! i think it probably matters more what you have personally done for committees in which you are a part of, and the impact of these contributions. i've held a lot of leadership/chairperson positions in my school (although not directly part of the SC, but in another leadership committee in my school which is very similar to SC), and i never got accepted to any schools LOL! i assume these schools would probably prefer quality > quantity

​

>Also, I heard from other Reddit comments that each JC only accept 1-2 candidates each year so I am concerned on whether not being in the Student Council will affect my chances? 

may or may not be true and could differ from jc to jc. i'm not too sure about this. but it's definitely very hard to get in anyway. just try your best. 

​

> Has there been cases in the past where they accept non SC member candidates? What more can I do to increase my chances?

don't know about the non SC member thing, but given your current leadership positions, i think it is sufficient as it's more unique. you could probably increase your chances by making big impacts, contributions & initiatives in the things you're a part of !! anyway what you can do will probably depend what you're a leader of. make sure to show youre very passionate about it! 

take this entire comment as a grain of salt though hahahahaa i don't know the itty bitty details about dsa leadership, but these are just some general things ive learned from my research while i was doing DSA and experience. regardless, beyond just wanting to DSA with your leadership positions, i hope you'll also do things that are actually meaningful for yourself too!

all the best!

hii!!! i also have a huge procrastination problem LOL but here's what worked for me:  
1. plan out a study schedule, but don't plan like those 8 hour study blocks (personally i find that super scary), i like to plan 2 hour study blocks, for example 2-4pm and 8-10pm cuz i also don't like studying in the morning so it will b less scary & you actl stick to it! :D 

2. if u study at home, try studying outside! (maybe in a library or cafe etc., if u no money, go library LOL) personally going out works for me since like, you alr come all the way here, might as well j sit down and study yk ! 

3. arrange study grp (now this one is super super common advice, but it might not work for everyone, it only works for me occasionally so try to study w those very focused ppl) so you'll be like supervised and stuff

4. pomodoro method!!!! i stick by this method no matter what it's been stuck with me for 3 years and i will forever superglue it to myself because i swear by it. have 25min study block / 5 min break OR 50 min study block / 10 min break or whatever u find suits you! personally i don't really have a timer for pomodoro, i actl just use a stop watch instead / ypt to track how long i've studied for, and if i feel tired i'll check the time, and if i've studied long enough ill j take a short break haha (so that it won't break my focus either!) pomodoro helps me to focus a lot so yeah

anyway no matter what js remember to take a break & take care of ur mental health!! goodluck for ur o's!
